The experimental erosion tests were conducted on 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.5875 mm Inconel 718 coupons coated with EB-PVD 7YSZ.
The erosion rate was defined as the ratio of the measured coated sample erosion mass loss to the mass of erosive particles impacting the surface.
The particle restitution characteristics were measured using high-speed photography and Particle Image Displacement Velocimetry (PIDV).
The experimentally-derived erosion rate correlation showed the erosion rate increased with impingement angle, impact velocity, and temperature.
The maximum erosion rate for the EB-PVD TBC coating occurred at a 90 degree impingement angle, while the maximum for the Inconel 718 substrate occurred between 20-30 degrees.
The computational simulations used an Euler-Lagrangian two-stage, one-way particle interaction approach with RANS flow solutions.
The experimentally-based erosion and restitution models were implemented as user-defined functions in the ANSYS CFX software.
For the commercial APU turbine, the simulations predicted the highest local TBC erosion rate of 72.94 mg/g/cm^2 on the rotor suction side.
The overall TBC erosion rates for the commercial APU turbine were predicted to be 0.83 mg/g for the stator and 0.87 mg/g for the rotor.
Particle seeding only within 5% of the stator span at the hub and shroud resulted in concentrated erosion bands on the stator pressure surface.
The paper does not provide detailed comparisons of the results between the different turbine designs studied.
The experimental techniques and computational methodology were the main focus of the paper, rather than a comprehensive analysis of the erosion patterns in the different turbines.
The paper does not explicitly discuss the key assumptions and limitations of the computational approach used.
The experimentally-derived erosion and restitution models were critical for predicting the TBC erosion on the turbine blade surfaces.
The combined experimental and computational approach allowed for a more comprehensive investigation of TBC erosion in turbomachinery.
